body.text: Kṣaṇabhaṅgasidviḥ vyatirekātmikā /
body.translated_text: Proof of Momentariness (<s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) in the Form of Negative Concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) /

children.translated_text: The <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) in the form of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) implies the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) /
In the dissimilar instance (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>), it is stated that when existence (<s>sattva</s>) is present, the reason [applies] //

body.text: yatsattat kṣaṇikaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ santaścāmīvivādāspadībhūtāḥ padārthā iti svabhāvo hetuḥ / na tāvadasyāsidviḥ sambhavati / yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣānumāṇapramāṇapratīte dharmmiṇi sattvaśabdenābhipretasyārthakriyākāritvalakṣaṇasya sādhanasya pramāṇasamadhigatatvāt / na ca virudvānaikāntikate / vyāpakānupalambhātmanā viparyyayabādhakapramāṇena vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt / byāpakañcārthakriyākāritvasya kramākramikāryyaviṣayatvameva / na punaḥ kāraṇagatau kāryyagatau vā kramākramāvasya vyāpakau / kṛtvā karaṇalakṣaṇasya kramasya kṣaṇike 'sambhavāt / kāryyagatābhyāṃ kramākramābhyāṃ kāraṇaśaktervyāptayogāt / tasmāt kāraṇagatayā kramākramikāryyaviṣayatayā vyāpyamānā kāraṇaśaktiḥ kramākramavyāptetyucyate / viṣayeṇa viṣayinirddeśāt / vyavahāralāghavārthaṃ / tataśca yadyapi sarvvatra kramākramau sattvasya vyāpakāvityādyucyate / tathāpi kramākramikāryyaviṣayatvameva vyāpakaṃ bodvavyaṃ / nanu yadaikameva kāryyamaṅkurādikamutpadyate, tadā kathaṃ kāryyagatakramākramavyavastheti cet /
body.translated_text: Whatever exists is momentary, just as a pot — and these objects that have become the locus of dispute are existent — thus the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is the reason. Firstly, its unestablishedness is not possible, because the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) — characterized by causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), which is intended by the word 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>) — is established through a means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) with respect to the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) that is cognized through perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>) as appropriate. Nor is there the defect of being contradicted or inconclusive, because the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is established through a counter-proof (<s>viparyyayabādhaka-pramāṇa</s>) in the form of non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>). And the pervader of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) is precisely the capacity for effects that are sequential or simultaneous — not that sequence and simultaneity with respect to the cause or with respect to the effect are themselves the pervaders. Because sequence, which has the character of a causal operation (<s>karaṇa</s>), is impossible in a momentary entity. Because there is no connection of pervasion between the causal capacity and the sequence-and-simultaneity pertaining to the effect. Therefore, the causal capacity, being pervaded by the capacity for effects that are sequential or simultaneous — which pertains to the cause — is called 'pervaded by sequence and simultaneity,' the possessor of the object being designated by the object, for the sake of economy of expression. And thus, although everywhere it is said 'sequence and simultaneity are the pervaders of existence,' nevertheless, what should be understood as the pervader is precisely the capacity for effects that are sequential or simultaneous. Now, if only a single effect such as a sprout arises, then how is the determination of sequence and simultaneity with respect to the effect [established]? — if such be the objection:

body.text:
ucyate / yadyapyekameva kāryyaṃ bhinnakālakāryyamapekṣyakramastadabhāvāccākrama statkāritvameva kramākramakāritvaṃ / tathāpyapekṣaṇīyaviṣayabhedāt kramākramayorasāṅkaryyameva / pitṛputratvavat / kaḥ punarasau vyāptiprasādhako vyāpakānupalambha iti cet / ucyate / yasya kramākramikāryyaviṣayatvannāsti, na tat śaktaṃ, yathā śaśaviṣāṇaṃ / nāsti ca nityābhimatasya bhāvasya kramākramikāryyaviṣayatvamiti vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / na tāvadayamasidvo vaktavyaḥ / nityasya dharmmiṇaḥ kramākramikāryyaviṣayatvena vyāpakena saha virodhasadbhāvāt, tathā hi pūrvvāparakālayorekatve nityatvaṃ kṣaṇadvayepi bhede kramākramitvaṃ / tataśca nityatvaṃ kramākramitvañcetyabhinnatvaṃ bhinnatvañcetyuktaṃ bhavati / etayośca parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇatayā virodhaḥ / tat kathaṃ nitye kramākramasambhavaḥ / nāpi virudvaḥ sapakṣe bhāvāt / nacānaikāntikaḥ / kramākramābhāvasyārthakriyāsāmarthyābhāvena vyāptatvāt / tathā hi na tāvat kramākramābhyāmanyaḥ prakārosti, yenārthakriyāsambhāvanāyāṃ kāramākramābhyāmarthakriyāvyāptirna syāt / tasmādarthakriyāmātrānubadvatayā tayoranyataraprakārasya / ubhayorabhāve cābhāvādarthakriyāmātrasyeti tābhyāṃ tasya vyāptisidviḥ / pakṣīkṛte ca tayorabhāvenārthakriyāśaktyabhāvasidvau kathamanekāntaḥ / na hi byāpyavyāpakayorvyāpyavyāpakabhāvasidvimudvūyabyāpyābhāvena vyāpakābhāvasya vyāptisidvau, upāyāntaramastīti niravadyo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / sattvasya kṣaṇikatvena vyāptiṃ sādhayatyeva / nanu vyāpakānupalambhataḥ sattvasya kathaṃ svasādhyaprativandhasidviḥ, asyāpyanekadoṣaduṣṭatvāt / tathāhi na tāvadayaṃ prasaṅgo hetuḥ sādhyadharmmiṇi pramāṇasidvatvāt, parābhyupagamasidvatvābhāvāt, viparyyayaparyyavasānābhāvācca / atha svatantraḥ, tadāśrayāsidvaḥ / akṣaṇikasyāśrayasyāsambhavādapratītatvādvā / pratīti rhi pratyakṣeṇānumānena vikalpamātreṇa vā syāt / prathamapakṣadvaye sākṣātpāramparyyeṇa vā svapratītilakṣaṇārthakāritve maulaḥ sādhāraṇo hetuḥ / vyāpakānupalambhaśca svarūpāsidvaḥ syāt / arthakriyākāritve kramākramayoranyatarasyāvaśyambhāvāt / antimapakṣe tu na kaścidveturanāśrayaḥ syāt vikalpamātrasidvasya dharmmiṇaḥ sarvvatra sulabhatvāt / api ca tat kalpanājñānaṃ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvi vā syāt, liṅgajanma vā, saṃskārajaṃ vā, sandigdhavastukaṃ vā, avastukaṃ vā / tatrādyapakṣadvaye 'kṣaṇikasya sattaivābyāhatā kathaṃ vādhakāvatāraḥ / tṛtīye tu na sarvvadā 'kṣaṇikasattāniṣedhaḥ / tadarpitasaṃskārābhāve tat smaraṇāyogāt / caturthe tu sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ hetudoṣaḥ / pañcame ca tadviṣayasyābhāvo na tāvat pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati / akṣaṇikātmanaḥ sarvvadaiva tvanmate 'pratyakṣatvāt / na cānumānatastadabhāvaḥ
pratibadvaliṅgānupalambhādityāśrayāsidvistāvadudvatā / evaṃ dṛṣṭāntopi pratihantavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: [Reply:] It is said: Even though the effect is one, [the cause] is sequential in relation to effects at different times and simultaneous in the absence of that [temporal difference] — its being a producer is itself its being a sequential-and-simultaneous producer. Even so, because the objects to be considered are different, there is no confusion between sequential and simultaneous [production] — just as in the case of father and son. Now, what is the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) that establishes the pervasion? It is said: Whatever does not have the character of being the object of sequential and simultaneous effects is not capable — like a hare's horn. And the entity considered to be permanent does not have the character of being the object of sequential and simultaneous effects — this is the non-apprehension of the pervader. This should not be called unestablished, because there is actual contradiction between the permanent subject (<s>dharmin</s>) and the pervader consisting of being the object of sequential and simultaneous effects. For thus: permanence consists in the identity of the earlier and later times, while being sequential-and-simultaneous consists in difference even across two moments. Therefore, saying 'permanence and being sequential-and-simultaneous' amounts to saying 'identity and difference.' And since these abide in mutual exclusion, there is contradiction. Then how can the sequential and simultaneous occur in a permanent [entity]? Nor is [this reason] contradictory, because it is present in the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>). Nor is it inconclusive, because the absence of sequential-and-simultaneous [production] is pervaded by the absence of the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>). For there is no other mode besides sequential and simultaneous, by which, while causal efficacy is possible, the pervasion of causal efficacy by sequential-and-simultaneous [production] would not hold. Therefore, since either of the two modes invariably accompanies any causal efficacy whatsoever, and since in the absence of both there is absence of causal efficacy itself, the pervasion of causal efficacy by them is established. And when their absence in the thesis-subject establishes the absence of the capacity for causal efficacy, how can there be inconclusiveness? For when the pervasion between the pervaded and the pervader is established, and the absence of the pervader establishes the absence of the pervaded, there is no other method — thus the non-apprehension of the pervader is faultless. It indeed establishes the pervasion of existence with momentariness. [Objection:] How does the non-apprehension of the pervader establish the connection of [existence] with its own property to be proved, given that this [argument] too is afflicted with many defects? For firstly, this is not a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) type of reason, because it is established by a means of proof in the thesis-subject, because it is not established merely through the opponent's acceptance, and because it does not culminate in the reversal [of the consequence]. If it is an independent [reason], then it suffers from unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>), because a non-momentary basis is impossible or not cognized. For cognition [of the basis] would be either through perception, through inference, or through mere conceptual construction. In the first two options — whether directly or indirectly — there would be the original common reason [fallacy] regarding the capacity for causal efficacy as characterized by one's own cognition. And the non-apprehension of the pervader would suffer from unestablishedness of its own form, because either sequential or simultaneous [production] necessarily accompanies causal efficacy. In the last option, no reason would lack a basis, since a subject established through mere conceptual construction is easily available everywhere. Furthermore, that conceptual cognition would be either post-perceptual, or inference-born, or memory-born, or of doubtful object, or objectless. In the first two options, the very existence of the non-momentary is uncontested — how then can invalidation enter? In the third, the denial of non-momentary existence is not universally applicable, because in the absence of impressions deposited by that [perception], remembering it would be impossible. In the fourth, doubtful basis is a defect of the reason. In the fifth, the non-existence of its object cannot be established through perception, because on your view the non-momentary is always imperceptible. Nor [can] its non-existence [be established] through inference — because the inferential mark connected [with the probandum] is not apprehended — thus the unestablishedness of the basis remains. The example should be refuted in the same way.

body.text: svarūpāsidvopyayaṃ hetuḥ sthirasyāpi kramākramisahakāryyapekṣayā kramākramābhyāmarthakriyopapatteḥ / nāpi kramayaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ / tathāhi kramisahakāryyapekṣayā kramikāryyakāritvantāvadavirudvaṃ /
body.translated_text: This reason also suffers from unestablishedness of its own form (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), because even for a stable [entity], causal efficacy is possible through sequential and simultaneous means in dependence on sequential and simultaneous cooperative causes (<s>sahakārin</s>). Nor does the defect stated in the options of sequential and simultaneous [production] arise. For producing sequential effects in dependence on sequential cooperative causes is not contradictory.

body.text: tathāca śaṅkarasya saṃkṣipto 'yamabhiprāyaḥ / sahakārisākalyaṃ hi sāmarthyaṃ / tadvaikalyañcāsāmarthyaṃ / na ca tayorāvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyāntadvataḥ kācit kṣatiḥ, tasya tābhyāmanyatvāt / tatkathaṃ sahakāriṇo 'napekṣyakāryyakaraṇaprasaṅga iti /
body.translated_text: And thus, the summarized view of <s>Śaṅkara</s> is as follows: The completeness of auxiliary causes (<s>sahakāri-sākalya</s>) is indeed capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>), and their incompleteness is incapacity. And the entity itself suffers no harm from the appearance and disappearance of those [auxiliary causes], since it is different from them. How then could there be the absurd consequence of producing effects without depending on auxiliary causes?

body.text: trilocanasyāpyayaṃ saṃkṣiptārthaḥ / kāryyameva hi sahakāriṇamapekṣate / na kāryyotpattihetuḥ / yasmāddvividhaṃ sāmarthyannijamāgantukañca sahakāryyantaraṃ / tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavatsahakārinānātvādapi kramavatkāryyanānātvopapatteraśakyaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratikṣaṇamanyānyatvamupapādayitumiti //
body.translated_text: The summarized meaning of <s>Trilocana</s> is also this: It is the effect itself that depends on auxiliary causes, not the cause of the effect's arising. Because capacity is of two kinds — innate (<s>nija</s>) and adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>) — requiring another auxiliary cause. Therefore, even for a non-momentary entity, since the diversity of effects can be explained by the diversity of successive auxiliary causes, it is impossible to establish that things are different from moment to moment.

body.text: nyāyabhūṣaṇo 'pi lapati / prathamakāryyotpādanakāle hyuttarakāryyotpādanasvabhāvaḥ / ataḥ prathamakāla evāśe ṣāṇi kāryyāṇi kuryyāditi cet / tadidaṃ mātā me vandhyetyādivat svavacanavirodhādayuktaṃ / yohyuttarakāryyajananasvabhāvaḥ sa kathamādau tatkāryyaṃ kuryyāt / na tarhi tatkāryyakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ / nahi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikamapi karotīti //
body.translated_text: <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> also argues: If at the time of producing the first effect, [the cause] has the nature of producing subsequent effects, then it should produce all effects at the very first moment. [Reply:] This is untenable due to self-contradiction, like saying 'my mother is barren.' For that which has the nature of producing a subsequent effect — how could it produce that effect at the outset? Then it would not have the nature of producing that [subsequent] effect. For that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and so forth.

body.text: vācaspatirapi paṭhati / nanvayamakṣaṇikaḥ svarūpeṇa kāryyañjanayati / taccāsya svarūpaṃ tṛtīyādiṣviva kṣaṇeṣu dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe saditi tadāpi janayet / akurvvan vā tṛtīyādiṣvapi na kurvvīta / tasya tādavasthyāt / atādavasthye vā tadevāsya kṣaṇikatvaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s> also states: 'But this non-momentary entity produces effects through its own nature. And that nature of its exists in the second moment just as in the third and subsequent moments. So it should produce [the effect] then too. Or, if it does not produce [it], it should not produce [it] in the third and subsequent moments either, since its condition remains the same. But if its condition does not remain the same, that itself constitutes its momentariness.'

body.text: atrocyate / satyaṃ svarūpeṇa kāryyañjanayati na tu tenaiva / sahakārisahitādeva tataḥ kāryyotpattidarśanāt / tasmāt vyāptivatkāryyakāraṇabhāvo 'pyekatrānyayogavyavacchedenāmyatrāyogavyavacchedenāvabodvavyaḥ / tathaiva lokikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ sampratipatteriti na kramikāryyakāritvapakṣoktadoṣāvasaraḥ //
body.translated_text: To this we reply: It is true that [the cause] produces effects through its own nature, but not by that [nature] alone, since the arising of effects is observed only from [a cause] accompanied by auxiliary causes. Therefore, like <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance), the cause-effect relation too should be understood through the exclusion of connection with one [set of conditions] and the exclusion of non-connection with another. This is precisely the consensus of both ordinary people and investigators. Hence there is no scope for the faults raised against the position of successive effect-production.

body.text: nāpyakṣaṇike yaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣāvakāśaḥ / ye hi kāryyamutpāditavanto dravyaviśeṣāsteṣāṃ vyāpārasya niyatakāryyotpādanasamarthasya niṣpādite kāryye 'nuvarttamāneṣvapi teṣu dravyeṣu nivṛttārthādūnā sāmagrī jāyate / tatkathaṃ niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayiṣyati / na hi daṇḍādayaḥ svabhāvenaiva karttāro yenāmī niṣpatterārabhya kāryyaṃ vidadyuḥ / kintarhi vyāpārāveśinaḥ / na ceyatā svarūpeṇa na karttāraḥ svarūpakārakatvanirvvāhaparatayā vyāpārasamāveśāditi //
body.translated_text: Nor is there scope for the faults stated against the position of simultaneity in the case of a non-momentary entity. For those particular substances that have produced an effect — their operation, which is capable of producing a determinate effect, having completed the effect, even though those substances continue to persist, a diminished aggregate arises, its purpose being fulfilled. How then will it produce again what has already been produced? For it is not the case that the stick and other [instruments] are agents by their very nature, such that they would create the effect from the moment of their completion. Rather, they are [agents] through the entrance of operation. And it is not that, insofar as they are not agents through their own nature, the [objection] is aimed at establishing that agency is through their own nature, [but rather] it is through the entry of operation.

body.text: kiñca kramākramābhāvaśca bhaviṣyati na ca satvābhāva iti sandigdhavyatirekopyayaṃ vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / na hi kramākramābhyāmanyaprakārasyābhāvaḥ sidvaḥ / viśeṣaniṣedhasya śeṣābhyanujñāviṣayatvāt / kiñca prakārāntarasya dṛśyatvenātyantaniṣedhaḥ / adṛśyatve tu nāsattāniścayo viprakarṣiṇāmiti na kramākramābhyāmarthakriyāsāmarthyasya vyāptisidviḥ / ataḥ sandigdhavyatireko 'pi vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / kiñca dṛśyādṛśyasahakāripratyayasākalyavataḥ kramayaugapadyasyātyantaparokṣatvāt tena vyāptaṃ sattvamapi parokṣameveti na tāvatpratibandhaḥ pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati nāpyanumānataḥ, tatpratibadvaliṅgābhāvāditi / api ca kramākramābhyāmarthakriyākāritvaṃ vyāptamityatisubhāṣitaṃ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, there will be the absence of succession and simultaneity, but not the absence of existence — so this inference through non-apprehension of the pervader also has doubtful negative concomitance. For the absence of a mode other than succession and simultaneity is not established, since a specific negation has as its scope the permission of the remainder. Furthermore, if the other mode is visible, there is absolute negation [only of what is visible]; but if it is invisible, there is no certainty of its nonexistence for those remote [from perception] — therefore the establishment of the pervasion of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā-sāmarthya</s>) by succession and simultaneity is not accomplished. Hence this inference through non-apprehension of the pervader also has doubtful negative concomitance. Moreover, since succession and simultaneity, [dependent on] the totality of visible and invisible auxiliary conditions, are utterly beyond [direct] perception, existence pervaded by them is also beyond perception — therefore the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is not established through perception, nor through inference, due to the absence of a logical mark that is [itself] necessarily connected with that [pervasion].

body.text: yadi krameṇa vyāptaṃ kathamakrameṇa / athākrameṇa na tarhi krameṇa; kramākramābhyāṃ vyāptamiti tu brūvata vyāpterevābhāvaḥ pradarśito bhavati / nahi bhavati / agnirdhūmabhāvābhāvābhyāṃ vyāpta iti / ato vyāpteranaikāntikatvam / api ca kimidaṃ vādhakamakṣaṇikānāmasattāṃ sādha yati, utasvit, akṣaṇikāt sattvasya vyatirekaṃ, atha sattvakṣaṇikatvayoḥ prativandhaṃ / na pūrvvo vikalpaḥ / uktakrameṇa hetorāśrayāsidvatvāt / na ca dvitīyaḥ / yato vyāpakanivṛttisahitā vyāpyanivṛttirvyatirekaśabdasyārthaḥ / sā ca yadi pratyakṣeṇa pratīyate tadā tadvetuḥ syāditi sattvamanaikāntikaṃ / vyāpakānupalambhaḥ svarūpāsidvaḥ / atha sā vikalpyate / tadā pūrvvoktakrameṇa pañcadhā vikalpya vikalpyo dūṣaṇīyaḥ / ata eva na tṛtiyo 'pi vikalpaḥ / vyatirekāsidvau sambandhāsidveḥ / kiñca na bhūtalavadatrākṣaṇiko dharmmī dṛśyate / na ca svabhāvānupalambhe vyāpakānupalambhaḥ kasyacit dṛśyasya pratipattimantareṇāntarbhāvayituṃ śakya iti / kiñcāsyābhāvadharmmatve / āśrayā sidvatvamitaretarāśrayatvañca / bhāvadharmmatve virudvatvañca / ubhayadharmmatve cānaikāntikatvamiti na trayīndoṣajātimatipatati //
body.translated_text: If [existence] is pervaded by sequential [production], how can it be [pervaded] by simultaneous [production]? And if by simultaneous, then not by sequential. But one who says 'it is pervaded by both sequential and simultaneous' demonstrates the very absence of pervasion. For one cannot say 'fire is pervaded by both the presence and absence of smoke.' Now, if [it is said that existence is] pervaded by sequential-or-simultaneous, and thus not [pervaded] by [mere] sequential alone — then let us examine whether this alternative [disjunctive] property is real or merely constructed. If real, it must be established by a means of proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>). [But] not by perception, because the disjunction is not perceivable. Nor by inference, because the inferential mark is unestablished. For the property of being 'sequential-or-simultaneous' as a disjunct is not cognized in [any specific] subject. If it is said to be a mere conceptual construction: is the contradiction [with permanence] real or merely constructed? It is not a real contradiction, because the contradictory [terms] are merely constructed — like the contradiction of a barren woman's son. If the contradiction too is merely constructed, then the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) of existence [with non-momentariness] is not ultimately [established].

body.text: yatpunaruktamakṣaṇikatve karmayaugapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhāditi / tatra virodhasidvimanusaratā virodhyapi pratipattabyaḥ / tatpratītināntarīyakatvāt virodhasidveḥ / yathā tuhinadahanayoḥ sāpekṣadhruvabhāvayośca pratiyogī cākṣaṇikaḥ pratīyamānaḥ pratītikāritvāt sanneva syāt ajanakasyāprameyatvāt / saṃvṛttisidvenākṣaṇikatvena virodhasidviriti cet / saṃvṛtisidvamapi vāstavaṃ kālpanikaṃ vā syāt / yadi vāstavaṃ kathantasyāsattvaṃ kathañcārthakriyāvirodhaḥ / arthakriyāṃ kurvvadvi vāstavamucyate /
body.translated_text: As for the further statement that in the case of non-momentariness, causal efficacy does not contradict sequential and simultaneous [production] — therein, one who follows [the establishment of] contradiction must also ascertain the contradictory [entity], because the establishment of contradiction necessarily requires its cognition. Just as with cold and heat: the contradiction is established only in dependence on [cognizing both].

body.text: atha kālpanikaṃ / tatra kiṃ virodho vāstavaḥ kālpaniko vā / na tāvadvāstavaḥ kalpitavirodhivirodhatvāt / bandhyāputravirodhavat / atha virodho 'pi kālpanikaḥ / na tarhi sattvasya vyatirekaḥ pāramārthika iti kṣaṇabhaṅgo dattajalāñjaliriti / ayameva codyaprabandho 'smad gurubhiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ //
body.translated_text: Now, if [the contradiction is] merely constructed: is the contradiction real or merely constructed? Not real, because [the contradictories] are themselves constructed — like the contradiction of a barren woman's son. If the contradiction too is merely constructed, then the negative concomitance of existence is not ultimate.

body.text: nityannāsti na vā pratītiviṣayastenāśrayāsiddhatā / hetoḥ svānubhavasya cākṣatirataḥ kṣiptaḥ sapakṣo 'pi ca / śūnyaśca dvitīyena sidhyati na cāsattāpi sattā yathā no nityena virodhasidvirasatā śakyā kramāderapīti //
body.translated_text: "A permanent [entity] either does not exist or is not an object of cognition — hence the basis of the reason is unestablished. One's own experience [of it] too is impaired, and thus even the positive example is discarded. Empty too [is the argument] — it is established by the second [consideration], and non-existence is not existence; just as the establishment of contradiction through a permanent [entity] — nor can non-existence be accomplished."

body.text: atrocyate / iha vastunyapi dharmmidharmmavyavahāro dṛṣṭoyathā gavi gotvaṃ, paṭe śuklatvaṃ turage gamanamityādi / avastunyapi dharmmidharmmavyavahāro dṛṣṭo yathā śaśaviṣāṇe tīkṣṇatvābhāvo bandhyāputre vakratvābhāvo gagaṇāravinde gandhābhāva ityādi / tatrāvastuni dharmmittvannāstīti kimbastudharmmeṇa dharmmitvannāsti / āhosvidavastudharmmeṇāpi / prathamapakṣe sidvasādhanaṃ dvitīyapakṣe tu svavacanavirodhaḥ / yadāhu rguravaḥ /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: In the case of real entities too, the conventional usage of property and property-possessor is observed — as [for example] cowness in a cow, whiteness in a cloth, movement in a horse, and so forth. In the case of non-entities too, the conventional usage of property and property-possessor is observed — as [for example] the absence of sharpness in a hare's horn, the absence of knowledge in a barren woman's son.

children.translated_text: "Is the establishment by a means of proof of some property in a non-entity,
or the convention of invalidation and affirmation, present here or not?
If it is present somewhere, how do these refutations not [apply]?
If it is entirely absent, [there is] the establishment of the self-contradiction of one's own words."

body.text: avastuno dharmmitvasvīkārapūrvvakatvasya vyāpakasyābhāve āśrayāsidvidūṣaṇasyānupanyāsaprasaṅgaityarthaḥ / yenaiva hi vacanenāvastuno dharmmitvābhāvena dharmmeṇa dharmmatvamabhyupagataṃ / parastu pratiṣidhyata iti vyaktamdimīśvaraceṣṭitaṃ / tathāhyavastuno dharmmitvannāstīti vacanena dharmmitvābhāvaḥ kimavastu vidhīyate, anyatra vā, na vā kvacidapīti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning is: in the absence of the pervader — namely, the prior acceptance of property-bearerhood (<s>dharmitva</s>) for a non-entity (<s>avastu</s>) — there would be the absurd consequence of not presenting the refutation of unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>). For by the very statement through which property-bearerhood is accepted — via the property of absence of property-bearerhood in a non-entity — while the other side is refuted, this is clearly demonic behavior [i.e., self-contradictory]. For thus: through the statement 'a non-entity does not have property-bearerhood,' the absence of property-bearerhood — is it predicated of the non-entity itself, or elsewhere, or nowhere at all? These are the three alternatives.

body.text: prathamapakṣe 'vastuno na dharmmitvaniṣedhaḥ / dharmmitvābhāvasya dharmmasya tatraiva vidhānāt / dvitīye 'vastuni kimāyātaṃ / anyatra dharmmitvābhāvavidhānāt / tṛtīyastu pakṣo vyartha eva nirāśrayatvāt iti kathamavastuno dharmmitvaniṣedhaḥ / tasmādyathā pramāṇopanyāsaḥ prameyasvīkārapūrvvakatvena vyāptaḥ / vācakaśabdopanyāso vā vācyasvīkārapūrvvakatvena vyāptaḥ / tathāvastuno dharmmitvaṃ nāstīti vacanopanyāso 'vastuno dharmmitvasvīkārapūrvvatvena vyāptaḥ / anyathā tadvacanopanyāsasya vyarthatvāt / tadyadi vacanopanyāso vyāpyadharmmaḥ / tadāvastuno dharmmitvasvīkāropi vyāpakadharmmo durbbāraḥ / atha na vyāpakadharmmaḥ / tadā vyāpyasyāpi vacanopanyāsasyāsambhava iti mūkataivātra balādāyāteti kathaṃ na svavacanavirodhasidviḥ / nahyabrūvan parambodhayitumīśaḥ / bruvan vā doṣamimaṃ pariharttumiti mahati saṅkaṭe praveśaḥ / avastuprastāve sahṛdayāṇāṃ mūkataiva yujyata iti cet / aho mahadvaidagdhyaṃ / avastuprastāve svayameva yathāśakti valgitvā bhagno mūkataiva nyāyaprāpteti paribhāṣayā niḥsarttumicchati / nacāvastuprastāvo rājadaṇḍena vinā caraṇamarddanādināniṣṭimātreṇa vā pratiṣedvuṃ śakyate / tataścātrāpi kramākramābhāvasya sādhanatve sattvābhāvasya ca sādhyatve sandigdhavastubhāvasyāvastyātmano vā kṣaṇikasya dharmmitvaṃ kena pratihanyate / trividho hi dharmmo dṛṣṭaḥ kaścidvastuniyato nīlādiḥ / kaścidavastuniyato yathā sarvvopākhyāvirahaḥ / kaścidubhayasādhāraṇo yathānupalabdhimātraṃ / tatra vastudharmmeṇāvastuno dharmmitvaniṣedha iti yuktaṃ / natvavastudharmmeṇa / vastvavastudharmmeṇa vā / svavacanasyānuyanyāsaprasaṅgādityarkṣāṇakasyābhāve sandehe vāvastudharmmeṇa dharmmitvamavyāhatamiti nāyamāśrayāsidvo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the first alternative, there is no denial of property-bearerhood to the non-entity, because the property consisting of the absence of property-bearerhood is itself predicated right there [in the non-entity]. In the second, what has befallen the non-entity? — since the absence of property-bearerhood is predicated elsewhere. The third alternative is simply pointless, being without a basis. Therefore, how can property-bearerhood be denied to a non-entity? Thus, just as the presentation of a means of proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is pervaded by the prior acceptance of what is to be proved (<s>prameya</s>), and just as the presentation of a denoting word is pervaded by the prior acceptance of the denoted [meaning], so too the presentation of the statement 'a non-entity does not have property-bearerhood' is pervaded by the prior acceptance of property-bearerhood for a non-entity. Otherwise, the presentation of that statement would be pointless. Therefore, if the presentation of the statement is the pervaded property, then the prior acceptance of property-bearerhood for a non-entity is also the pervading property and is unavoidable. But if [it is] not the pervading property, then the presentation of the statement, which is the pervaded, would also be impossible — and thus muteness would forcibly ensue here. How then is there not the establishment of self-contradiction? For one who does not speak cannot inform the opponent, and one who speaks cannot avoid this fault — thus one enters a great impasse. [Objection:] 'In the context of non-entities, silence is indeed appropriate for the wise.' — Oh, what great cleverness! Having oneself prattled as best one could in the context of non-entities, and having been defeated, one wishes to escape by the rule 'silence is the logical conclusion!' But the context of non-entities cannot be prevented without royal punishment, or merely by treading on one's feet or other unpleasant acts. Therefore, even here — where the absence of sequence and simultaneity (<s>kramākramābhāva</s>) is the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), and the absence of existence (<s>sattvābhāva</s>) is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — what prevents the property-bearerhood of the momentary entity (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), whether its entity-hood is doubtful or it is of the nature of a non-entity? For properties are observed to be of three kinds: some are restricted to entities, such as blue and the like; some are restricted to non-entities, such as the absence of all designation; and some are common to both, such as mere non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhimātra</s>). Among these, it is proper to deny property-bearerhood to a non-entity by means of an entity-property, but not by means of a non-entity-property, nor by means of a property common to both entity and non-entity — because of the absurd consequence that one's own statement would also not be presented. Therefore, in the absence of certainty [that the subject is a non-entity], or in doubt, property-bearerhood through a non-entity-property remains unimpaired. Thus this non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) does not suffer from unestablished basis.

body.text: akṣaṇikāpratītā vayamā śrayāsidvoheturiti tu yuktamuktaṃ / tadapratītau tadvyavahārāyogāt / kevalamasau vyavahārāṅgabhūtā pratīti rvastvavastunorekarūpā na bhavati / sākṣātpāramparyyeṇa vastusāmarthyabhāvinī hi vastupratītiḥ / yathā pratyakṣamanumānaṃ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvī ca vikalpaḥ / avastunastu sāmarthyābhāvāt vikalpamātrameva pratītiḥ / vastuno hi vastubalabhāvinī pratīti ryathāsākṣātpratyakṣaṃ paramparayā tatpṛṣṭhabhāvī vikalpo 'numānañca / avastunastu na vastubalabhāvinī pratītistatkārakatvenāvastutvahāniprasaṅgāt / tasmādvikalpamātramevāvastunaḥ pratītiḥ / nahyabhāvaḥ kaścidvigrahavān yaḥ sākṣātkarttavyo 'pi tu vyavaharttavyaḥ / sa ca vyavahāro vikalpādapi sidhyatyeva / anyathā sarbbajanaprasidvo 'vastuvyavahāro na syāt / iṣyate ca tadvarmitvapratiṣedhānuvandhādityakārakenāpi vikalpamātrasidvo 'kṣaṇikaḥ svīkarttavya iti nāyamapratītatvādapyāśrayāsidvoheturvaktavyaḥ / tataścākṣaṇikasya vikalpamātrasidvatve yaduktaṃ na kaścidveturanāśrayaḥ syadvikalpamātrasidvasya dharmmiṇaḥ sarvvatra sulabhatvāditi tatasaṅgataṃ / vikalpamātrasidvasya dharmmiṇaḥ sarvvatra sambhave 'pi vastudharmmeṇa dharmmitvāyogāt / vastudharmmahetutvāpekṣayā āśrayāsidvasyāpi hetoḥ sambhavāt / yathā ātmano vibhutvasādhanārthamupanyastaṃ sarvvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvāditi sādhanaṃ / vikalpaścāyaṃ hetūpanyāsāt / pūrvvaṃ sandigdhavastukaḥ, samarthite tu hetāvavastuka iti brūmaḥ / na cātra sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ nāma hetudoṣaḥ / āstāntāvat / sandigdhasyāvastunopi vikalpamātrasidvasyāvastudharmmāpekṣayā dharmmitvaprasādhanāt / vastudharmmahetutvāpekṣayaiva sandigdhāśrayasya hetvābhāsasya vyavasthāpanāt / yatheha nikuñje mayūraḥ kekāyitāditi / avastukavikalpaviṣayasyāsattvantu vyāpakānupalambhādeva prasādhitaṃ / evaṃ dṛṣṭāntasyāpi vyomāderdvarmmitvaṃ vikalpamātreṇa pratītiścāvagantavyā / tadevamavastudharmmāpekṣayāvastunodharmmitvasya vikalpamātreṇa pratīteścāpanhotumaśakyatvānnāyamāśrayāsidvo hetuḥ / na dṛṣṭāntakṣatiḥ //
body.translated_text: As for the statement that 'the non-momentary is not cognized, hence the reason has an unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>)' — that is indeed rightly said. For in the absence of its cognition, there could be no convention regarding it. However, this cognition, which serves as a component of convention, is not of a single form for real and unreal [entities]. For the cognition of a real entity arises through the power of the real entity, either directly or indirectly — as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and conceptual cognition following upon perception. But for an unreal entity, since there is no [causal] power, cognition is through mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) alone. For the cognition of a real entity arises through the force of reality — directly as perception, and indirectly as conceptual cognition following upon it and as inference. But for an unreal entity, there is no cognition arising from the force of reality, because if it were caused by [something real], there would be the absurd consequence of its ceasing to be unreal. Therefore, the cognition of an unreal entity is through mere conceptual construction alone. For no absence is an entity with a body that could be directly perceived; rather, it is to be conventionally dealt with. And that convention is accomplished even from conceptual construction alone. Otherwise, the convention regarding unreal entities that is universally acknowledged by all people would not exist. And since it is accepted [by the opponent] — because of the connection with the negation of possessing that property — even the opponent must unwillingly accept the non-momentary as established through mere conceptual construction. Therefore, this reason should not be called one with an unestablished basis merely because [the non-momentary] is not [perceptually] cognized. And since the non-momentary is thus established through mere conceptual construction, the statement that 'no reason would lack a basis, since a subject established through mere conceptual construction is easily available everywhere' is indeed apt. [But we reply:] Even though a subject established through mere conceptual construction is available everywhere, it cannot be a subject of a property that is a real property (<s>vastudharma</s>). Because, insofar as the reason is a real property, even a reason with an unestablished basis is possible. Just as the proof presented for establishing the omnipresence of the self — 'because it possesses qualities apprehended everywhere' — is a proof, and this conceptual construction, through the presentation of the reason, was previously of doubtful reality; but when the reason is validated, we say it is of unreal [basis]. And here, the defect of doubtful basis (<s>sandigdhāśrayatva</s>) is not a fault of the reason. Set that aside. [The point is:] even for a doubtful [basis], or even for one that is unreal and established through mere conceptual construction, the status of being a subject is to be established with respect to unreal properties. The determination that a doubtful basis constitutes a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) holds only with respect to reasons that are real properties. As in [the inference]: 'There is a peacock in this thicket, because of the cry' [where the basis is doubtful]. And the non-existence of what is the object of conceptual construction about unreal entities has already been established through the very non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>). In the same way, the status of the example — such as space and the like — as a subject, and its cognition through mere conceptual construction, should be understood. Thus, since the status of an unreal entity as a subject with respect to unreal properties, and its cognition through mere conceptual construction, cannot be denied — this reason does not have an unestablished basis. Nor is there damage to the example.

body.text: na caiṣa svarūpāsidvaḥ / akṣaṇike dharmmiṇi kramākramayo rvyāpakayorayogāt / tathā hi yadi tasya prathame kṣaṇe dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryyakāraṇasāmarthyamasti tadā prathamakṣaṇabhāvikāryyavat dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvyapi kāryyaṃ kuryyāt / samarthasya kṣepāyogāt / atha tadā sahakārisākalyalakṣaṇasāmarthyaṃ nāsti / tadvaikalyalakṣaṇasyāsāmarthyasya sambhavāt / na hi bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa karotīti svarūpeṇaiva karoti / sahakārisahitādeva tataḥ kāryyotpattidarśanāt iti cet / yadā tāvadamī mīlitāḥ santaḥ kāryyaṃ kurvvate tadaikārthakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvameṣāmastu ko ni ṣedvā / militaireva tu tatkāryyaṅkarttavyamiti kuto labhyate / pūrvvāparakālayorekasvabhāvatvāt bhāvasya / sarvvadā jananājananayoranyataraniyamaprasaṅgasya durvvāratvāt / tasmāt sāmagrījanikā naikaṃ janakamiti sthiravādināmmanorājyasyāpyaviṣayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is this [reason] unestablished in its own form (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), because in a non-momentary subject, the pervaders — sequential and simultaneous [production] — are impossible. For thus: if at the first moment [the entity] possesses the capacity to cause effects belonging to the second and subsequent moments, then, just as it produces effects belonging to the first moment, it should produce effects belonging to the second and subsequent moments as well — because delay is impossible for what is capable. If, on the other hand, at that time the capacity characterized by the completeness of cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārisākalya</s>) does not exist — because incapacity characterized by their incompleteness is possible — [the objector says:] 'It is not that an entity produces by its own nature alone; rather, the arising of the effect is observed only from that [entity] combined with cooperative conditions.' [We reply:] When these [causes], having come together, produce the effect — let that cooperative causality of theirs, characterized by accomplishing a single purpose, be theirs; who can deny it? But from where is it obtained that only the combined [causes] must produce that effect? Because the entity has one and the same nature at earlier and later times, the absurd consequence of being invariably fixed in either always-producing or always-not-producing is unavoidable. Therefore, [the claim that] 'the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) is the producer, not a single producer' is beyond even the aspirations of the permanentists (<s>sthiravādin</s>).

body.text: kiṃ kurmmo dṛśyate tāvadevamiti cet / dṛśyatāṃ kintu pūrvvasthitādeva paścāt sāmagrīmadhyapraviṣṭādbhāvāt kāryyotpattiranyasmādeva viśiṣṭasāmagrīsamutpannāt kṣaṇāditi vivādapadametat / tatra prāgapi sambhave sarvvadaiva kāryyotpatte rnavā kadācidapīti virodhamasamādhāya tata eva kāryyotpattiriti sādhyānuvādamātrapravṛttaḥ kṛpāmarhati /
body.translated_text: 'What can we do? It is observed to be so.' — If so, let it be observed; but that the production of the effect occurs from the very [entity] that previously existed, having entered into the aggregate of [cooperative] conditions later — or from another [entity] entirely, one that has arisen from the particular aggregate of conditions at that [later moment] — this is the point of dispute. Therein, one who, without resolving the contradiction that, if [production] were possible even earlier, the effect would always arise, or never at all, resorts to [saying] 'the effect arises from that very [previous entity]' — engaging in mere restatement of the thesis (<s>sādhyānuvāda</s>) — deserves compassion.

body.text: na ca pratyabhijñānādevaikatvasidviḥ / tat pauruṣasya lūna punarjjātakeśakuśakadalīstambādau nirddalanāt / vistareṇa ca pratyabhijñānadūṣaṇamasmābhiḥ sthirasidvidūṣaṇe pratipāditamiti tata evāvadhāryyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Nor is the unity [of the entity across time] established through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>). That [argument from recognition] has been demolished — in [cases of] hair that falls and regrows, <s>kuśa</s> grass, plantain stalks, and the like [which are recognized as the same but are in fact different]. And the detailed refutation of recognition has been presented by us in the 'Refutation of the Proof of Permanence' (<s>Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇa</s>) — it should be ascertained from there.

body.text: nanu kāryyameva sahakāriṇamapekṣate / na tu kāryyotpattihetuḥ / yasmāddvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijamāgantukañcasahakāryyantaraṃ / tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavat sahakārinānātvādapi kramavatkāryyanānātvamiti cet, bhavatu tāvannijāgantukabhedena dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ tathāpi tatprātisvikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇaṃ sadyaḥ kriyādharmmakamavaśyābhyupagantavyam / tadyadi prāgapi, prāgapi kāryyaprasaṅgaḥ / atha paścādeva na tadā śthirobhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: If it is objected: 'It is the effect that requires a cooperative cause, not the cause of the effect's production. For capability is of two kinds — intrinsic and adventitious (through another cooperative cause). Therefore, even for a non-momentary [entity], just as there is multiplicity of effects due to multiplicity of cooperative causes in sequential [production], so too [there would be no contradiction]' — let there indeed be two kinds of capability, intrinsic and adventitious. Even so, the particular real entity (<s>vastusvalakṣaṇa</s>) belonging to that [entity] must necessarily be accepted as having the property of immediate activity. If [it has immediate activity] even earlier, then there would be the absurd consequence of the effect [arising] earlier too. If only later, then the entity is not permanent.

body.text: na ca kāryyaṃ sahakāriṇo 'pekṣata iti yuktaṃ / tasyāsattvāt / hetuśca sannapi yadi svakāryyannakaroti tadā tatkāryyameva tanna syāt, svātantryāt / yaccoktaṃ / yo 'hyuttarakāryyajananasvabhāvaḥ sa kathamādau kāryyaṃ kuryyāt / na tarhi tatkāryyakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ / na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikamapi karotīti / tadasaṅgataṃ / sthirasvabhāvatve bhāvasyottarakālamevedaṃ kāryyannapūrvvakālamiti kuta etat / tadabhāvācca kāraṇamapyuttarakāryyakaraṇasvabhāvamityapi kutaḥ / kiṃ kurmma uttarakālameva tasya janmeti cet / sthiratve tadanupapadyamānamasthiratāmādiśatu / śthiratve 'pyeṣa eva svabhāvastasya yaduttarakṣaṇa eva kāryyaṃ karotīti cet / na / pramāṇavādhite svabhāvābhyupagamāyogāditi na tāvadakṣaṇikasya kramikāryyakāritvamasti / nāpyakramikāryyakāritvasambhavaḥ / dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe kārakasvarūpasadbhāve punarapi kāryyakaraṇaprasaṅgāt / kāryye niṣpanne tadviṣayavyāpārābhāvādūnā sāmagrī na niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayediti cet / na / sāmagrīsambhavāsambhavayorapi sadyaḥ kriyākārakasvarūpasambhave janakatvamavāryyamiti prāgeva pratipādanāt / kāryyasya hi niṣpāditatvāt punaḥ karttumaśakyatvameva kāraṇamasamarthamāvedayati / tadayamakṣaṇike kramākramikāryyakāritvābhāvo na sidvaḥ / na ca kramākramābhyāmaparaprakārasambhavo yena tābhyāmavyāptau sandigdhavyatireko hetuḥ syāt / prakārāntaraśaṅkāyāṃ tasyāpi dṛśyādṛśyatvaprakāradvayadūṣaṇe 'pi svapakṣepyanāśvāsaprasaṅgāt / tasmādanyo 'nyavyavacchedasthitayornāparaḥ prakāraḥ sambhavati / svarūpāpraviṣṭasya vastuno 'vastunovānyatvāt / prakārā ntarasyāpi kramasvarūpāpraviṣṭatvāt / tathātīndriyasya sahakāriṇo 'dṛśyatvepyayogavyavacchedena dṛśyasahakārisahitasya dṛśyasyaiva sattvasya dṛśyakramākramābhyāṃ vyāptiḥ pratyakṣādeva sidhyati / evaṃ kramākramābhyāmarthakriyākāritvaṃ byāptamiti kramākramayoranyo 'nyavyavacchedena sthitatvādetatprakāradvayaparihāreṇārthakriyākāritvamanyatra na gatamityarthaḥ / ata evaitayorvinivṛttau nivartteta /
body.translated_text: Nor is it proper [to say] that the effect depends on [merely] the cooperative cause. Because that [cooperative cause] is non-existent [at the earlier time]. And if the cause, though existent, does not produce its own effect, then that would not be its effect at all — due to its independence [from the cause]. And as for what was said — 'how could that whose nature is to produce a later effect produce an effect at the beginning? It is simply not of the nature of producing that [first] effect. For one whose nature is to produce blue does not produce yellow and the like' — this is incoherent. For if the entity has a permanent nature, whence comes [the restriction that] 'this effect belongs only to the later time and not to the earlier time'? And in the absence of that [restriction], whence [the claim] that 'the cause too has the nature of producing only later effects'? 'What can we do? Its production is simply at the later time.' — If this is inexplicable given permanence, let it indicate impermanence. 'Even given permanence, this is simply its nature — that it produces the effect only at the later moment.' — No, because it is improper to accept a nature that is contradicted by a means of proof. Thus, firstly, a non-momentary [entity] does not have the capacity for sequential effect-production. Nor is there the possibility of simultaneous effect-production, because if the nature of being a producer exists in the second moment as well, there would be the absurd consequence of production occurring again. 'When the effect has been accomplished, due to the absence of activity regarding that object, the aggregate [of conditions] is deficient and would not accomplish what has [already] been accomplished.' — No, because it has already been demonstrated that when the nature of being an immediate producer exists, regardless of whether the aggregate is complete or incomplete, productiveness cannot be prevented. For the very fact that the effect, having been produced, cannot be produced again reveals that the cause is incapable. Thus, the absence of sequential and simultaneous effect-production in a non-momentary [entity] is not established. Nor is there any other mode beyond sequential and simultaneous, by which, if pervasion by these two fails, the reason would have doubtful negative concomitance. The suspicion of another mode, when subjected to the refutation of both the visible and invisible varieties, would also create unease in one's own position. Therefore, no other mode is possible beyond those two that abide in mutual exclusion — because anything not included in the nature of [the entity] is something other, whether a real or unreal entity; and that alternative mode too is not included in the nature of sequence. Likewise, even though supersensory cooperative causes are invisible, through the exclusion of the impossible, the pervasion of visible existence alone with visible sequential-and-simultaneous [production], together with visible cooperative causes, is established through perception alone. Thus, causal efficacy is pervaded by sequential-and-simultaneous [production]; and since the sequential and the simultaneous abide in mutual exclusion, causal efficacy that excludes both of these modes does not exist elsewhere — this is the meaning. Therefore, when both are absent, [causal efficacy] too would cease.

body.text:
trilocanasyāpi vikalpatraye prathamadūṣaṇamāśrayāsidvidoṣaparihārato nirastaṃ / dvitīyañcāsaṅgataṃ vikalpajñānena vyatirekasya pratītatvāt / nahyabhāvaḥ kaścit vigrahavān yaḥ sākṣātkarttavyo 'pi tu vikalpādeva vyavaharttavyaḥ / na hyabhāvasya vikalpādanyāpratipattirapratipattirvā sarvvathobhayathāpi tadvyavahārahāniprasaṅgāt / evaṃ vaidharmmyadṛṣṭāntasya hetuvyatirekasya ca vikalpādeva pratītiḥ / tṛtīyamapi dūṣaṇamasaṅgataṃ / vyāpakānupalambhe nirddoṣatvasya kṣaṇikatvena vyāpteravyāhatatvāt /
tadayaṃ vyāpakānupalambho 'kṣaṇikasyāsattvaṃ, sattvasya tato vyatirekaṃ kṣaṇikatvena vyāptiñca sādhayatyekavyāpārātmakatvāt iti sthitaṃ /
body.translated_text:
As for <s>Trilocana's</s> [objections] too: among his triad of alternatives, the first criticism is set aside by the removal of the defect of unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>). The second is also untenable, because the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is cognized through conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpajñāna</s>). For absence is not some embodied thing that is to be directly perceived; rather, it is to be dealt with only through conceptual construction. For it is not the case that an absence is cognizable only through something other than conceptual construction, or that it is not cognizable [at all] — because in either case there would be the absurd consequence of the abandonment of all discourse about it. Likewise, the cognition of the dissimilar instance (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) and of the absence of the reason (<s>hetuvyatireka</s>) is also through conceptual construction alone. The third criticism is also untenable, because the pervasion of faultlessness by momentariness remains uncontradicted in the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>).
Thus it is established that this non-apprehension of the pervader proves in a single operation the nonexistence of the non-momentary, the negative concomitance of existence from that [non-momentary], and the pervasion [of existence] by momentariness.

body.text: nanu vyāpakānupalabdhiriti yadyanupalabdhimātrantadā na tasya sādhyabudvijanakatvamavastutvāt / na cānyopalabdhirvyāpakānupalabdhirabhidhātuṃ śakyā bhūtalādivat anyasya kasyacidanupalabdheriti cet tadasaṅgataṃ / dharmmyupalabdherevānyatrāpyanupalabdhitayā vyavasthāpanāt / yathā neha śiṃśapā vṛkṣābhāvādityatra vṛkṣāpekṣayā kevalapradeśasya dharmmiṇa upalabdhirdṛśyānupalabdhiḥ / śiṃśapāpekṣayā ca kevalapradeśasya dharmmiṇa upalabdhireva śiṃśapābhāvopalabdhiriti svabhāvahetuparyyavasāyivyāpāro vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / tathā hi nityasya dharmmiṇo vikalpabudvyadhyavasi tasya kramikāritvākramikāritvāpekṣayā kevalagrahaṇameva kramikāritvā kramikāritvānupalambha arthakriyāpekṣayā ca / kevalapratītirevārthakriyāviyogapratītiriti vyāpakānupalambhāntarādasya na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If the non-apprehension of the pervader is merely non-apprehension, then it cannot generate the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), since it is not a real thing. And the apprehension of something else cannot be called 'non-apprehension of the pervader,' because — as in the case of a bare ground and such — any other thing could [equally] be non-apprehended. [Reply:] This is untenable, because the apprehension of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) itself is determined to function as a non-apprehension elsewhere [too]. Just as in the case 'there is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree here, because of the absence of a tree' — the apprehension of the bare location as <s>dharmin</s> with respect to 'tree' is a <s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the perceptible); and the apprehension of the bare location as <s>dharmin</s> with respect to '<s>śiṃśapā</s>' is itself the apprehension of the absence of <s>śiṃśapā</s> — thus the non-apprehension of the pervader is an operation that culminates in a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (reason based on essential nature). To elaborate: with respect to the permanent <s>dharmin</s> as determined by conceptual cognition, the mere apprehension [of the dharmin] alone, in relation to its being a sequential producer and a simultaneous producer, constitutes the non-apprehension of sequential and simultaneous production; and in relation to causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), the mere cognition [of the dharmin] alone constitutes the cognition of disconnection from causal efficacy. Thus there is no difference between this and other forms of the non-apprehension of the pervader.

body.text: adhyavasāyāpekṣayā ca vāhye 'kṣaṇike 'vastuni vyāpakābhāvāt vyāpyābhāvasidvivyavahāraḥ / adhyavasāyaśca samanantarapratyayavalāyātākāraviśeṣayogādagṛhīte 'pi pravarttanaśaktirvodvavyaḥ / īdṛśaścādhyavasāyo 'rtho 'smaccitrādvaitasidvau nirvvāhitaḥ / sa cāvisambādī vyavahāraḥ pariharttumaśakyaḥ; yadvyāpakaśūnyaṃ; tadvāpyaśūnyamiti / etasyaivārthasyānenāpi krameṇa pratipādanāt / ayañca nyāyo yathā vastubhūte dharmmiṇi tathāvastubhūte 'pīti ko viśeṣaḥ / tathāhyekajñānamātravikalpa eva / yathā ca, hariṇaśirasi tenaikajñānasaṃsargiśṛṅgamupalabdhaṃ / śaśaśirasyapi tena sahaikajñānasaṃsargitvasambhāvanayaiva śṛṅgaṃ niṣidhyate / tathā nīlādāvapariniṣṭhitanityānityabhāve kramākramau svadharmmiṇā sārdvaṃ ekajñānasaṃsargiṇau dṛṣṭau nitye 'pi yadi bhavataḥ / nityagrāhiṇā jñānena svadharmmiṇā nityena sahaiva gṛhyeyātāmiti sambhāvanayā / ekajñānasaṃsargidvārakameva pratiṣidhyate / kathaṃ punaretannityajñāne kramākramayorasphuraṇamiti / yāvatā kramākramakroḍīkṛtameva nityaṃ vikalpayāma iti cet / ataeva vādhakāvatāro viparītarūpāropamantareṇa tasya vaiyarthyāt / kālāntareṇaikarūpatayā nityatvaṃ / kramākramau ca kṣaṇadvaye bhinnarūpatayā / tato nityatvasya kramākramikāryyaśakteśca parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatayā durvvāro virodha iti kathaṃ nitye kramākramayorantarbhāvaḥ / anantarbhāvācca śuḍvanityavikalpena dūrīkṛtakramākramasamāropeṇa kathamullekhaḥ / tataśca pratiyogini nitye 'pi kalpyamāne, ekajñānasaṃsargilakṣaṇaprāpte nityopalabdhireva nityavirudvasyānupalabhyamānasya kramākramasyānupalabdhiḥ / tataeva vārthakriyāśakteranupalabdheḥ / tasmādvyāpakavivekidharmmyupalabdhitayā na vyāpakānupalambhāntarādasya viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: And with respect to the ascertainment (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), since the pervader is absent in the external non-momentary non-entity, the convention of the absence of the pervaded is established. And the ascertainment — due to the possession of a specific form brought about by the force of the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), even when the [real object] has not been grasped — should be understood as the power to impel practical engagement. And such an ascertainment as an object has been demonstrated in our <s>Citrādvaitasiddhi</s> (Proof of Variegated Non-Duality). And this non-contradictory convention cannot be rejected: 'whatever is devoid of the pervader is devoid of the pervaded.' For it is the presentation of this very meaning through this very procedure. And this logical principle — how does it differ whether the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) is real or unreal? For it is merely a single-cognition conceptual construction. And just as a horn, being an object associated with a single cognition on the head of a deer, is observed, so too on the head of a hare, by the mere possibility of association with a single cognition, the horn is negated. Likewise, in blue and the like, where the permanent-impermanent status is not definitively established, sequence and simultaneity (<s>kramākrama</s>) are observed as being associated with a single cognition along with their own <s>dharmin</s>. If they also existed in the permanent — they should be grasped by the cognition grasping the permanent, along with the permanent <s>dharmin</s>, by the mere possibility [of such association]. It is precisely through the medium of single-cognition association that they are negated. [Objection:] 'But how is it that sequence and simultaneity do not manifest in the cognition of the permanent?' — inasmuch as we conceptualize the permanent precisely as incorporating sequence and simultaneity. [Reply:] It is precisely for this reason that invalidation enters — because without the superimposition of an opposed form, that [conceptualization] would be pointless. For permanence is identity across different times, while sequence and simultaneity involve difference across even two moments. Therefore, since permanence and the capacity for sequential-and-simultaneous effects exist in a relationship of mutual exclusion, the contradiction is unavoidable — so how can sequence and simultaneity be included within permanence? And in the absence of such inclusion, how can there be any mention [of them] through a pure permanent-concept that has cast aside the superimposition of sequence and simultaneity? Therefore, even when the permanent is postulated as a counter-correlate, the apprehension of the permanent, which has the character of being associated with a single cognition, is itself the non-apprehension of the sequence and simultaneity that are contradictory to permanence and are not apprehended. And from that very [non-apprehension] follows the non-apprehension of the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāśakti</s>). Therefore, this is not different from another non-apprehension of the pervader, being in the form of the apprehension of a <s>dharmin</s> that is discriminated from the pervader (<s>vyāpakavivekin</s>).

body.text: nanvetadavastudharmmikopayogikastvadhiṣṭhānatvāt pramāṇavyavasthāyā iti cet / kimidambastvadhiṣṭhānatvannāma / kimparamparayāpi vastunaḥ sakāśādāgatatvam, atha vastuni kenacidākāreṇa vyavahārakāraṇatvaṃ, vastubhūtadharmmiprativadvatvambā /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'But this is useful [only] for a non-entity <s>dharmin</s>, because the validity of <s>pramāṇa</s> has its basis in a real entity (<s>vastu</s>).' — What is this 'having a real entity as basis' (<s>vastvadhiṣṭhānatva</s>)? Is it having come, even indirectly, from a real entity? Or is it being a cause of convention with respect to a real entity through some form? Or is it being a counter-correlate to a real-entity <s>dharmin</s>?

body.text: yadyādyaḥ pakṣastadā kramākramasyārthakriyāyāśca vyāptigrahaṇagocaravastuprativadvatvamapi na kṣīṇaṃ / na ca dvitīye 'pi pakṣe doṣaḥ sambhavati / kṣaṇabhaṅgivastusādhanopāyatvādasya / na cāntimo 'pi vikalpaḥ kalpyate / tasyaiva nityavikalpasya vastuno dharmmibhūtasya kramākramavadvāhyanityopādānaśūnyatvenārthakriyāvadvāhyanityopādānaśūnyatvaprasādhanāt / paryyudāsavṛttyā budvisvabhāva bhūtā kṣaṇikākāre vastubhūte dharmmiṇi prativadvatvasambhavāt /
body.translated_text: If the first alternative, then the grasping of the pervasion of sequence-and-simultaneity with causal efficacy — its having a real entity as counter-correlate — is also not exhausted. Nor is there any fault even in the second alternative, because this [argument] is a means of establishing a momentary real entity. Nor should the last alternative be imagined, because that very permanent-concept — since the real entity that is its <s>dharmin</s> is devoid of an external permanent substratum possessing sequence and simultaneity — [the argument] establishes that it is devoid of an external permanent substratum possessing causal efficacy. Through an implicative negation (<s>paryudāsa</s>), the property-bearerhood of the momentary form — which is a real entity that is of the nature of cognition — is possible.

body.text: ayameva nyāyo na vaktā bandhyāsutaścaitanyābhāvādityādau yojyaḥ / etena yathā vṛkṣābhāvādityādyantarbhāvayituṃ śakyo na tathāyamiti trilocano 'pi nirastaḥ /
body.translated_text: This very logical principle should be applied in [arguments such as] 'the speaker is not a barren woman's son, due to the absence of consciousness [in such a son]' and the like. By this, <s>Trilocana</s>'s [objection] too — 'this [argument] cannot be subsumed [under established types] in the way that [arguments like] "due to the absence of a tree" and the like can be subsumed' — is also refuted.

body.text: na ca kramādyabhāvastrayīṃ doṣajātinnātikrāmati / abhāvadharmmatve 'pyāśrayāsidvidoṣaparihārāt / yattvanena pramāṇāntarānnityānāmasattvasidvau kramādivirahasyābhāvadharmmatā na sidhyatītyuktaṃ / tadvālasyāpi durabhidhānaṃ / nityo hi dharmmī / asattvaṃ sādhyaṃ / kramikāryyakāritvākramikāryyakāritvaviraho hetuḥ / asya cābhāvadharmmatvannāma / asattvalakṣaṇasvasādhyāvinābhāvitvamucyate / tacca kramākrameṇa sattvasya vyāptisidvau sattvasya vyāpyasyābhāvena kramākramasya vyāpakasya viraho vyāptaḥ sidhyatītyabhāvadharmmatvaṃ prāgeva vidhyorvyāptisādhakāt pratyakṣādanumānātmakādvā pramāṇāntarāt sidva miti netaretarāśrayatvadoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: And the absence of sequence and the like does not exceed the triad of defects, because the defect of unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) is removed even when [the reason] has the character of a property of absence (<s>abhāvadharmatva</s>). As for the statement that 'when the non-existence of permanent [entities] is being established by another means of proof, the character of the absence of sequence and the like as a property of absence is not established' — that is also poorly stated, even for a child. For the permanent is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>); non-existence (<s>asattva</s>) is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum); the absence of producing sequential effects and of producing simultaneous effects is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). And the 'character of this as a property of absence' (<s>abhāvadharmatva</s>) means its invariable concomitance with its own <s>sādhya</s> characterized by non-existence. And this is established as follows: when the pervasion of existence (<s>sattva</s>) by sequence and simultaneity (<s>kramākrama</s>) is established, the absence of sequence and simultaneity — the pervader — is pervaded by the absence of existence — the pervaded. Thus the character as a property of absence is established even prior [to the present proof], from the independent means of proof that establishes the pervasion of the two positive [terms] — whether that be perception or inference — and therefore there is no defect of mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśrayatva</s>).

body.text: na ca sattāyāmivāsattāyāmapi tulyaprasaṅgo bhinna nyāyatvāt / vastubhūtaṃ hi tatra sādhyaṃ sādhanañca / tayodharmmyaipi vastubhūta eva yujyate //
body.translated_text: Nor is there an equal applicability (<s>tulyaprasaṅga</s>) to the proof of non-existence as there is to [the proof of] existence, because the methods are different. For there, both the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) are real entities. And the subject for both of those must also be a real entity.

body.text: vastunastu pratyakṣānumānābhyāmeva sidviḥ / tayorabhāve niyamenāśrayāsidviriti yuktaṃ / asattāsādhane tvavastudharmmā heturavastuni vikalpamātrasidve dharmmiṇi nāśrayāsidvidoṣeṇa dūṣayituṃ śakyaḥ / tathākṣaṇikasya kramayogapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhaḥ sidhyatyeva /
body.translated_text: But a real entity is established only through perception and inference. In their absence, unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) necessarily follows — this is correct. But in proving non-existence, a reason that is a non-entity property (<s>avastudharma</s>) in a subject established through mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) cannot be faulted with the defect of unestablished basis. Likewise, the contradiction of the non-momentary with causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) through sequence and simultaneity (<s>kramayogapadya</s>) is indeed established.

body.text: tathā vikalpādevākṣaṇiko virodhī sidvaḥ / vikalpollikhitaścāsya svabhāvo nāpara ityapi vyavaharttavyaṃ / anyathā tadanuvādena kramākramādirahitatvādiniṣedhādikamayuktaṃ / tat svarūpasyānullekhādityakṣaṇikaśaśaviṣāṇādiśabdānuccāraṇaprasaṅgaḥ / asti ca / ato yathā pramāṇābhāve 'pi vikalpasatvasya bandhyāsutādeḥsaundaryyādiniṣedho 'nurūpaḥ, tathā vikalpopanītasyaivākṣaṇika svarūpasya tat pratyanīkākāreṇa saha virodhavyavasthāyāṃ kīdṛśo doṣaḥ syāt / yadi cākṣaṇikānubhavābhāvāt virodhapratiṣedhaḥ, tarhi bandhyāputrādyananubhavādeva saundaryyādiniṣedho 'pi mābhūta /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the non-momentary, as contradictory, is established from conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) alone. And it should be understood that its nature is that which is outlined by conceptual construction, and no other. Otherwise, by appealing to it [the non-momentary], the negation of being devoid of sequence and non-sequence and so forth would be unjustified — [on the grounds] that its own nature is not outlined [at all] — and there would be the absurd consequence of not even uttering such words as 'non-momentary,' 'hare's horn,' and the like. But these are uttered. Therefore, just as the denial of beauty and so forth to a barren woman's son and the like, which exist only in conceptual construction, is appropriate even in the absence of a means of proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>), so too, what fault could there be in establishing the contradiction of the very nature of the non-momentary — as presented by conceptual construction — with its opposing form? And if the contradiction is denied because the non-momentary is not experienced, then the denial of beauty and the like to a barren woman's son and the like should also not hold, since they too are not experienced.

body.text: nanvevaṃ virodhasyāpāramārthikatvaṃ / taddvāreṇa kṣaṇabhaṅgasidvirapyapāramārthikī syāditi cet / na hi virodhonāma vastvantaraṃ kiñcit ubhayakoṭidattapādaṃ sambadvābhidhānamiṣyate 'smābhirupapadyate vā / yenaikasambandhino vastutvābhāve 'paramārthikaḥ syāt / yathā tviṣyate tathā pāramārthika eva / virudvābhimatayoranyo 'nyasvarūpaparihāramātraṃ virodhārthaḥ / tacca bhāvābhāvayoḥ pāramārthikameva na bhāvo 'bhāvarūpamāviśati / nāpyabhāvo bhāvarūpaṃ praviśatīti yo 'yamanayorasaṅkaraniyamaḥ sa eva pāramārthiko virodhaḥ / kālāntaraikarūpatayā hi nityatvaṃ / kramākramau kṣaṇadvaye 'pi bhinnarūpatayā tato nityatvakramākramikāryyakārakatvayorbhāvābhāvavat virodho 'styeva / nanu nityatvakramayaugapadyavattvañca virudvau vidhūya nāparo virodhonāma / kasya vāstavatvamiti cet / na / na hi dharmmāntarasya sambhavena virodhasya pāramārthikatvaṃ brūmaḥ / kintu virudvayordharmmayoḥ sadbhāve 'nyathā virodhanāmadharmmāntarasambhave 'pi yadi na virudvau dharmmau kva pāramārthikavirodhasadbhāvaḥ / virudvau ca dharmmau tāvataiva tāttviko virodhavyavahāraḥ / kimapareṇa pratijñāmātrasidvena virodhanāmnā vastvantareṇa / tadayaṃ pūrvvapakṣasaṃkṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, the contradiction would be non-ultimate (<s>apāramārthika</s>), and through it, the proof of momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) would also be non-ultimate. [Reply:] We neither accept nor find it possible that contradiction is some other real entity standing with feet planted in both sides. So it would not become non-ultimate merely because one of the related terms lacks real-entity-hood. Rather, as we accept it, it is indeed ultimate. The meaning of 'contradiction' for those held to be contradictory is merely the mutual exclusion of each other's nature. And this is indeed ultimate between existence and non-existence — existence does not enter the form of non-existence, nor does non-existence enter the form of existence — this invariable rule of their non-confusion is itself the ultimate contradiction. For permanence consists in identity of form across different times, while sequence and simultaneity consist in difference of form even across two moments. Therefore, between permanence and being a sequential-and-simultaneous producer of effects, there is contradiction, just as between existence and non-existence. [Objection:] Having negated both permanence and possessing sequential-and-simultaneous [production] as contradictory, there is no other [entity called] 'contradiction' — so whose reality [is in question]? [Reply:] No. For we do not assert the ultimacy of contradiction through the existence of some other property. Rather, when contradictory properties exist — if, even when some other property named 'contradiction' exists, the two properties are not contradictory — where is the existence of ultimate contradiction? And when two properties are contradictory, that alone suffices for the genuine convention of contradiction. What need is there for yet another real entity named 'contradiction,' established merely by assertion? This then is the summary of the opponent's position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).

children.translated_text: "A permanent [entity] either does not exist or is not an object of cognition — hence the basis of the reason is unestablished;

children.text: hetoḥ svānubhavasya ca kṣatirataḥ kṣiptaḥ sapakṣo 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: one's own experience of the reason too is impaired, and thus even the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is discarded;

children.text: śūnyaśca dvitayena sidhyati na vā sattāpi sattāyathā
children.translated_text: and it is empty [of establishment] by the second [alternative] — or existence is not [established]; just as, in the manner of existence,
the establishment of contradiction through a permanent [entity] — nor can the non-existence of sequence and the like be accomplished."

body.text: atra sidvāntasaṃkṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here is the summary of the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.translated_text: Whether, regarding a non-entity, the establishment of some property by a means of proof,
or the procedure of invalidation — does this obtain here or not?
If there is some [such procedure], how do these criticisms not apply?
And if there is none at all, then the self-contradiction of one's own statement is established.

body.text: tadevaṃ nityaṃ na kramikāryyakāritvākramikāryyakāritvayogiparamārthaḥ / tataśca sattāyuktamapi naiva paramārthataḥ / tataśca kṣaṇikākṣaṇikaparihāreṇa rāśyantarābhāvādakṣaṇikādvinivarttamānamidaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇikatva eva viśrāmyante na vyāptaṃ sidhyatīti sattvāt kṣaṇabhaṅgasidviṃravirodhinī //
body.translated_text: Thus, a permanent entity is not ultimately qualified for sequential-effect-production or simultaneous-effect-production. And consequently, even though possessed of existence, it is not so ultimately. And consequently, since there is no other category besides momentary and non-momentary, this existence, turning away from the non-momentary, comes to rest in momentariness alone. That the pervasion is established [follows] — thus the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) from existence (<s>sattva</s>) is uncontradicted.

children.translated_text: That understanding of the nature of all <s>dharmas</s> from which liberation is held [to arise] —
that very destroyer of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox opponents), the [doctrine of] momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>), has been established.
Through the invalidation [of the probandum's presence] in the dissimilar instance, the essential identity of the reason with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is established;
in establishing that, the twofold establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is here set forth.

body.text: iti vaidharmmyadṛṣṭānte vyatirekarūpavyāptyā kṣaṇabhaṅgasidviḥ samāptā // 0 //
body.translated_text: Thus the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) through <s>vyāpti</s> in the form of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) in the dissimilar instance (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) is completed. // 0 //

body.text: kṛtiriyaṃ mahāpaṇḍitaratnakīrttipādānām // 0 //
body.translated_text: This is the composition of the great <s>paṇḍita</s> <s>Ratnakīrti</s>. // 0 //
